author: Victor Dergunov
title: Amazon: Taking Over The World - Amazon.com, AMZN)
text:
Source: TechRaptor.com
Amazon ( AMZN ) has expanded almost exponentially over the past several years, and now commands one of the largest market caps out of any publicly traded company in the world. In fact, at a staggering market capitalization of $824 billion, Amazon is now second only to Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), and given the company's incredible growth rate, it is likely only a matter of time before Amazon becomes number one.
Not surprisingly, with returns of over 4,000% from 2008's lows, Amazon has been one of the top-performing stocks over the last decade. But how long can such stellar performance continue for? After all, Amazon is already one of the most valuable companies in the world. Some would even argue that it's "overvalued" by now.
Source: Nasdaq.com
Nevertheless, Amazon continues to grow aggressively, continuously challenging the status quo, and essentially reshaping the retail industry to fit its blueprint. In addition, the company continues to branch out into new segments and industries, and despite its somewhat frothy valuation, it has enormous profitability potential. So much so that the company's stock may not be that expensive relative to its next year's profitability prospects, thus Amazon's share price is likely to continue going higher from here.
Amazon's Aggressive Expansion Amazon has proven to be one of the most innovative companies the world has ever seen. The company continues to reshape the retail world, aggressively moving into new areas, constantly challenging the status quo, and always keeping competitors guessing. Let's not forget that Amazon started off as a small online bookstore operation, and has grown into one of the largest, most powerful, and most diversified business operations in the world.
Today, you can buy just about anything (within reason) on Amazon. As of the beginning of this year, Amazon had well over half a billion ( 562 million ) products selling on its website. But the modern Amazon is so much more than just an ecommerce juggernaut. It's a logistics empire , a content creator, a streaming giant, a cloud computing /services company, AI innovator , a hardware company, and a lot more.
Source: Scraphero.com
However, at the heart of Amazon is its Prime segment which offers streaming music, a "Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ) like" video service, free photo storage, and other perks, including free two-day shipping. Incredibly this service now has more than 100 million users , and at $12.99 per month, the annual revenues are likely to be over $15 billion from now. Moreover, the service helps keep consumers in the Amazon orbit, buying more products on its site, and using more of its products and services.
So, is Amazon a Monopoly? It's difficult to specifically classify Amazon as a monopoly, but approaching on 50% of total U.S. ecommerce sales certainly makes the internet giant an incredibly powerful force. Amazon is not simply sucking up market share from book stores and clothing retailers anymore. Amazon's reach has become extremely wide as the company strongly impacts electronic retailers, jewelers, all types of consumable manufacturers, high-end department stores, food delivery businesses, grocery stores, and even pharmacies and healthcare companies.
Source: Recode.net
Also, did you know that Amazon has quietly introduced a whole slew of its own in-house brands ranging from lingerie, to makeup, to home tools, men's shoes, clothing, tech accessories, food, furniture, and much more?
In addition, the company has also launched an exclusive line of about 60 different over-the-counter health products , sending a direct challenge to traditional pharmacies. And this is likely just the beginning of Amazon flexing its manufacturing and exclusivity muscles. In time, the company can put substantial pressure on competitors due to its enormous pricing flexibility.
So, is Amazon a "monopoly"? You tell me. What is becoming clear is that Amazon is essentially disrupting the whole retail world, not just a few segments of an industry.
Remarkable Revenue Growth Story Amazon has shown an extremely keen ability to grow revenues at an incredible scale and pace. In 2007 Amazon had fewer than $15 billion in revenues. 10 years later, the company increased revenues by more than 10-fold to nearly $178 billion, and the growth is not likely to end anytime soon. In fact, the company is expected to grow sales by over 33% this year to about $238 billion , and 2019 sales are likely to come in at about $300 billion. Beyond 2019, given the company's incredible momentum, only a significant global downturn will likely put a major dent in the company's revenue growth. Aside from that, Amazon's revenue growth is likely to remain above or around 20% for several years (4-7), possibly longer.
Source: Statista.com
Immense International Growth Potential The vast majority of Amazon's revenues still come from the U.S. In fact, about 65% of sales originate in the U.S. Nevertheless, Amazon is very active in international markets and is likely to grow international sales substantially going forward. In addition, Amazon is diversifying revenue streams away from retail, and this phenomenon will also continue to drive significant revenue growth.
Amazon: Growing International Market Share
Amazon: Diversifying Revenues
Amazon's Brand Value Amazon is now regarded ( by some sources ) as having the most valuable brand in the world. With a brand worth valued at over $150 billion, Amazon towers over most companies, and has even surpassed giants such as Apple and Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ). Its enormous brand value provides the company with more recognition and more power, which should translate into even more growth, pricing power, and overall influence.
Underestimated Earnings Potential People often discuss Amazon's elevated P/E multiple, and they sometimes use this excuse not to own the stock. Nevertheless, Amazon has plenty of levers it can use to become much more profitable in the future. Profits have never been a main objective for Amazon, growth has, but this does not mean the company can't monetize its businesses very effectively. It can, and it will when the time is right.
Just look at the Prime price hike, not a significant number of people are going to drop their Prime memberships due to a $2 a month increase. But the price hike will add billions to the company's bottom line, and the company can implement other profitability tactics to substantially increase net income in the future.
Just last quarter the company demolished earnings estimates, as Amazon reported EPS of $3.27 vs. estimates of just $1.26 , a 160% beat. An outstanding part was Amazon's AWS business which grew revenues at about 50% YoY, and brought in a massive $1.4 billion in operating income for the quarter.
To quote the CEO:
"AWS had the unusual advantage of a seven-year head start before facing like-minded competition, and the team has never slowed down. As a result, the AWS services are by far the most evolved and most functionality-rich."
Another noticeable bright spot is Amazon's advertising business, which saw revenues expand by about 140% YoY in the quarter to more than $2 billion. And then there is Prime, which grew revenues by a staggering 60% YoY to $3.1 billion.
When Amazon's businesses are firing on all cylinders and the company's revenue growth begins to slow down to about the low double digits, it will likely focus more on profitability to compensate for lower growth, whenever that may be. But for now, the company can still deliver significant profits, while growing at a rapid pace. In fact, Amazon has significantly surpassed its last three earnings reports by a combined $3.32 , which represents a 108% increase over consensus estimates.
This suggests that even now analysts are likely underestimating Amazon's earnings potential, and the company is likely to surprise higher going forward. In fact, analysts have been steadily moving EPS estimates higher for Amazon. Three months ago, consensus EPS estimates for this year were just $8.32 ; now they are $12.58. Next year's were $15.39; now they are $20.16. This trend of upward revisions is likely to continue as Amazon continues to surpass EPS estimates going forward.
Based on Amazon's EPS trend and continuous revenue growth coupled with higher-than-expected profitability, the company is likely to earn towards the upper end of next year's EPS range. This implies Amazon will likely earn around $30 per share next year. This indicates that given the company's current share price, Amazon is likely trading at just about 55 times forward earnings. And a forward P/E of 55 for a dominant company growing revenues at over 30% YoY, with substantial growth prospects remaining is not expensive in this market.
The Bottom Line Amazon continues to grow aggressively, has introduced an extensive line of in-house products, has a significant advantage in its AWS business, is continuously disrupting the retail world, and has created an entire "Amazon Economy", somewhat reminiscent of an online monopoly. This permits Amazon to manipulate pricing and control other factors that should ultimately provide the company with more power, revenue, and profits.
The company is already beginning to illustrate substantial profitability potential by surpassing its past three earnings results by significant margins. Future EPS is likely to come in higher than expected as well, and the company's rapid revenue growth is likely to remain around or above 20% for at least several more years.
The trend of upward EPS revisions is likely to continue and the company could realistically earn $30 per share next year, which puts Amazon's forward P/E at around 55, not expensive when compared to other fast growing, dominant market leaders likely to sustain growth for several or more years into the future.
Therefore, Amazon's stock is likely to continue higher until a significant market downturn arrives. Amazon will very likely become the first publically traded company to hit a trillion-dollar valuation and should surpass Apple as the world's most valuable publically traded company very soon.
